name: Calculating the Wage of an Employee at the Customer Service Call Center
description: Construct a program for the payment department of a company to calculate the wage of an employee who works at the customer service call center. Like other employees in the company, the employees at the customer service call center are paid based on the hours that they work. If they work over 40 hours in a week, the payment amount should take into account the overtime hours. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate.\nThe company's policy is to pay more to those employees at the customer service call center who work during weekends. Therefore, the minimum extra pay that the employees could receive for each day of work during weekends is $30. The extra pay increases to the maximum of $50 for the employees who have at least 5 days of work during weekends.
code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables which we need for this program
rate = 8.25 
standard = 40 
weekend_pay_min = 30 
weekend_pay_max = 50 
#Step 2: Read the input data
text = input("Enter the number of hours that the employee has worked: ")
hours = int(text)
text = input("Enter the number of days that the employee has worked during weekends: ")
no_weekend_days = int(text)
#Step 3: Pay overtime at "time and a half" of the regular rate of pay
if hours > standard :
    wage = standard * rate + ( hours-standard ) * ( rate * 1.5 )
else :
    wage = hours * rate
#Step 4: Take into account the extra pay for the work during weekends days
if no_weekend_days < 5 :
    wage += (no_weekend_days * weekend_pay_min)
else :
    wage += (no_weekend_days * weekend_pay_max)
#Step 5: Print the calculated wage
print("Wage:", wage)

1.content: #Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables which we need for this program

commentList: We need variable rate to store the regular hourly pay rate. We set it to 8.25, assuming that the employee receives $8.25 for each hour of work.
We need variable standard to store the standard hours in a work week. We set it to 40.
We need variable weekend_pay_min to store the minimum extra pay for the work during the weekend days. We set it 30.
We need variable weekend_pay_max to store the maximum extra pay for the work during the weekend days. We set it 50.

11.content: #Step 3: Pay overtime at "time and a half" of the regular rate of pay

commentList: To determine whether we should pay overtime to the employee, we need to test whether the employee has worked more than the standard hours in a work week. If the employee has worked more than the standard hours in a work week, then the payment should take into account the overtime hours and we need to pay overtime at "time and a half" of the regular rate of pay. Otherwise, we pay the employee based on the number of hours that the employee has worked and the regular pay rate.

The if statement tests whether the number of hours entered by the user is greater than the standard hours in a work week. If the number of hours is greater than the standard hours in a work week, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

When the number of hours is greater than the standard hours in a work week, we need to pay the employee for the standard hours in a work week plus the overtime hours that the employee has worked.

The standard hours in a work week are paid at a regular pay rate. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate. Therefore, the employee’s overtime rate of pay is the regular pay rate multiplied by 1.5.

If the above if test fails (i.e., when the employee has worked less than or equal to the standard hours in a work week), we should calculate the wage based on the number of hours that the employee has worked and the regular pay rate.

The statement inside the body of this else statement is executed when the if condition is false, i.e., the number of hours is less than or equal to the standard hours in a work week. Otherwise, the body of this else statement is skipped.
When there are no overtime hours, the wage is calculated based on the number of hours that the employee has worked and the regular pay rate.

16.content: #Step 4: Take into account the extra pay for the work during weekends days

commentList: The if statement tests whether the payment should take into account the minimum extra pay for working during weekend days. The payment should take into account the minimum extra pay when the employee has worked less than 5 days during weekend days.
If the number of days that the employee has worked during weekends is less than 5, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

When the number of days that the employee has worked during weekends is less than five, the minimum extra pay (i.e., $30) will be added to the employee's wage for each day that the employee has worked during the weekend.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable wage) and the result is stored in the variable wage. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement wage = wage + (no_weekend_days * weekend_pay_min).
If the above if test fails (i.e., when the employee has worked at least 5 days during weekend days), the payment should take into account the maximum extra pay for work during weekend days.

The statement inside the body of this else statement is executed when the if condition is false, i.e., when the employee has worked at least 5 days during weekend days. Otherwise, the body of this else statement is skipped.

When the number of days that the employee has worked during weekends is at least five, the maximum extra pay (i.e., $50) will be added to the employee's wage for each day that the employee has worked during the weekend.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable wage) and the result is stored in the variable wage. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement wage = wage + (no_weekend_days * weekend_pay_max).
